question.prompt:
Let \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) be the roots of the polynomial \(x^3 + kx + 1.\) What is the sum

\[ \begin{aligned} &a^3b^2 + a^2b^3 + b^3c^2 \\ &\quad {}+ b^2c^3 + c^3a^2 + c^2a^3? \end{aligned} \]

solutions.title: Complete a symmetric product
solutions.explanation:
The missing \(x^2\) term gives a useful relation among the roots. By Vieta's formulas,
\[
a+b+c=0,\qquad ab+bc+ca=k,\qquad abc=-1.
\]
Let \(S\) be the requested sum. The product
\[
(a+b+c)(a^2b^2+b^2c^2+c^2a^2)
\]
contains the six terms of \(S\), together with three extra terms. Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
0&=(a+b+c)(a^2b^2+b^2c^2+c^2a^2)\\
 &=S+a^2b^2c+ab^2c^2+a^2bc^2\\
 &=S+abc(ab+bc+ca)\\
 &=S+(-1)k.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(S=\boxed{k}\), choice \(\text{E}\).

solutions.title: Use root equations and power sums
